summary: Round 2 substantially closes the 4 highest-priority round-1 findings: (1) tasks/todo.md rewrite is now an explicit T8 deliverable with 8 enumerated v2 paths and is enforced by Acceptance Criteria line 541; (2) v2 critical paths gain a committed insight-skeleton-sample.json fixture (T1) and a manual Web Inspector verification path (T5); (3) T12 grew from 5 to 9 scenarios with 4 adversarial cases covering poisoned .md XSS, rapid double-click race, close-during-export, close-during-streaming; (4) Risks table now references T8/T12 expansions explicitly. These are real improvements and the deferral defensibility has materially increased. However, several round-1 sub-recommendations were not picked up and represent residual gaps that are still defensible per Decision 9 BUT should be acknowledged: (a) only ONE happy-path skeleton fixture committed — round 1 recommended 3+ malformed variants for fallback verification AND adversarial postMessage payload fixtures, neither delivered; (b) the 4 NEW T12 adversarial scenarios chose XSS+race+cancellation but skipped crash-recovery (kill process mid-stream, verify stale dir behavior) and large-tree export (30+ nodes) and blob URL revocation Web Inspector check — leaving 3 specific failure modes uncovered; (c) the Risks-table entry was edited but does NOT enumerate the 4 v2-specific risk classes (sandbox, atomic write, ZIP path safety, parallel cap) and does NOT pose the explicit upgrade-vs-defer question for PostMessageAllowlistTests + InsightCacheAtomicCRUDTests; (d) Task 11 description is unchanged from round 1 — still essentially identical to v1 Task 11, will likely produce a template-matched PASS; (e) sandbox/frameInfo/allowlist/topicIndex acceptance criteria still rely on grep — no runtime smoke tests added in T12 to verify runtime behavior matches static presence; (f) ZIP edge cases (non-zero exit codes other than 0, double-click Save, empty session, single-node-failure) not added; (g) vendored libs MANIFEST now covers all libs but no build-time integrity check enforces it. None of these gaps individually rise to critical for v2 ship — the 4 closed findings were the load-bearing ones. The remaining items are eligible for follow-up. No path REQUIRES a pre-merge XCTest that cannot be deferred, given (i) iframe sandbox + frameInfo defense-in-depth + CSP + connect-src 'none' provide layered defense for the security boundary, (ii) atomic write blast radius is bounded by per-session UUID dirs + cleanup, (iii) ZIP path safety is bounded by UUID-based node IDs (no user-controlled path component), (iv) parallel cap regression would manifest as 429 cascade in pre-deploy QA. RECOMMENDATION: ship-eligible after Task 11 description is strengthened (cheapest fix, prevents template-matched PASS) and 3 specific T12 additions are made (crash-recovery scenario, blob revocation Web Inspector check, KaTeX math content check). Remaining items can ship as documented follow-up.

findings.issue: Round 1 Finding 7 recommended strengthening Task 11 with 6 specific v2 re-derivation checks (todo.md v1-removal verification, T12 adversarial coverage check, NEW v2 fixtures count, runtime smoke supplement for 4 security boundaries, explicit upgrade/defer decision documented, M1 race carry-over status). Round 2 Task 11 description is essentially unchanged from round 1: 'Meta-audit: tests deferred per Decision 9. Verify tasks/todo.md follow-up scope expanded with v2-specific paths' + a leak-check sufficiency line. The risk identified in round 1 is unmitigated: Task 11 will produce a PASS by template-matching v1 Task 11 (same 5-check structure) without independently re-deriving whether v2's larger surface justifies the deferral. This is the cheapest gap to close (description-only edit) and the highest-leverage one (Task 11 is the gate on the entire deferral strategy).
findings.recommendation: Rewrite Task 11 description to explicitly require v2-specific evaluation: 'V2-specific test audit (NOT a template copy of v1 Task 11). Verify ALL of: (1) tasks/todo.md updated AND v1-only modules (InsightMarkerParserTests) explicitly removed, not just augmented; (2) Pre-deploy QA T12 adversarial coverage includes at minimum crash-recovery + navigate-during-stream + rapid-double-click + close-during-export — flag any missing; (3) NEW v2 fixtures committed: insight-skeleton-sample.json (happy) AND ideally 3+ malformed variants for fallback verification — flag if only happy fixture present; (4) for each of the 4 v2 security boundaries (sandbox attr, frameInfo guard, postMessage allowlist, topicIndex bounds), grep verification is supplemented with at least one runtime smoke check in T12 — flag if grep-only; (5) explicit decision documented (yes/no, with rationale) on whether PostMessageAllowlistTests + InsightCacheAtomicCRUDTests should be upgraded from follow-up to pre-merge given v2 surface — flag absence as a decision gap; (6) M1 race carry-over status: sectionId+topicIndex makes it more specific but not necessarily resolved — verify T12 (g) rapid-double-click test definitively resolves or documents as known. Write report logs/audit/test-audit.md with explicit FAIL gate if any of the 6 are unmet. Do NOT issue PASS by analogy to v1.'

findings.issue: Round 1 recommended 4 specific adversarial scenarios: (f) crash-recovery (kill MarkView mid-Phase-2, verify stale dir not contaminating fresh session), (g) navigate-during-stream race (breadcrumb-back + immediate deep-dive while sections in flight), (h) rapid double-click on deep-dive (M1-class race), (i) large-tree export (30+ nodes). Round 2 T12 added 4 adversarial scenarios but chose a different set: (f) poisoned .md XSS, (g) rapid double-click [matches recommended h], (h) close-during-export [matches part of recommended i but for cancellation, not large-tree], (i) close-during-streaming [matches recommended g cancellation aspect]. Three specific failure modes from round 1 are NOT covered by T12 round-2: (1) Crash-recovery: no scenario kills the MarkView process via Activity Monitor → Force Quit during Phase 2 streaming and verifies the next session uses fresh sessionUUID + ignores the stale dir + does not contaminate manifest. The Risks table line 521 claims 'next session uses fresh sessionUUID; stale dir from prior session ignored' but T12 does not test it. Atomic-write semantics are non-trivial; this is the only realistic way to verify them outside an XCTest target. (2) Large-tree export: exporting a 30+ node session is NOT in T12. The staging dir builder iterates over manifest entries — silent partial-failure semantics are unverified. (3) Blob URL revocation Web Inspector check: round 1 specifically called out a 6th scenario verifying URL.revokeObjectURL is called at session close. Without this, blob leaks of ~4MB per session can accumulate undetected. The poisoned-md (f) scenario IS valuable but it addresses a different gap (XSS sandbox boundary) than what round 1 recommended; both should be present.
findings.recommendation: Add 3 specific scenarios to T12: (j) Crash-recovery: open insight on TestFiles/, wait for Phase 1 + start of Phase 2, force-quit MarkView via Activity Monitor; restart, open insight on same folder; verify in Web Inspector + Finder that (i) new sessionUUID directory created, (ii) old session UUID directory persists in .insight-cache/ but is NOT read, NOT written to, NOT cleaned up automatically; (iii) manifest.json under new dir contains only new session nodes; document expected stale-dir disk usage in known-issues. (k) Large-tree export: programmatically build (via repeated deep-dive expansion or manual fixture insertion) a session with at least 30 nodes; click Save Archive; verify ZIP completes within 30s, opens in Safari, ALL nodes present, breadcrumb nav between local files works. Verify intermediate failure: corrupt one cached node HTML (rm + create empty), re-export, verify hard-fail with clear error rather than silent success with broken node. (l) Blob URL revocation: in Web Inspector → Memory → record snapshot before opening insight; open insight (loads ~4MB of blobs); take snapshot showing blobs in memory; close insight tab; take third snapshot; verify blobs are gone (not retained). If blobs persist after close, releaseInsightBlobs() is broken. Also add a short note to T12 about KaTeX math: open insight on a folder containing at least one .md file with KaTeX math (`$E = mc^2$` inline + block); verify math renders in iframe (resolves Risks-table 'KaTeX webfonts' validation owed since Decision 5).

findings.location: tech-spec.md Acceptance Criteria — Iframe sandbox security section (lines 559-567)
findings.issue: Round 1 Finding 5 recommended adding 4 runtime smoke tests to T12 to verify the sandbox/frameInfo/allowlist/topicIndex acceptance criteria correspond to actual runtime behavior, not just static grep matches. Round 2 added the poisoned-md scenario (T12 (f)) which exercises the sandbox + escape utility together, but does NOT add the 4 specific runtime checks recommended: (1) eval document.querySelector('iframe').sandbox.toString() in Web Inspector — assert exact string 'allow-scripts'; (2) inject test JS calling webkit.messageHandlers.bridge.postMessage from inside the iframe — verify either webkit.messageHandlers is undefined per sandbox semantics OR frameInfo guard rejects in Swift logs; (3) call window.postMessage with type='insightRequestNavigate' (not in allowlist) — verify parent rejects; (4) post insightDeepDiveClicked with topicIndex=-1, 999, null, '5' (string), {} — verify each rejected. The poisoned-md scenario covers some of (1) and (3) implicitly but does not enumerate negative cases for (2) and (4). Off-by-one errors in topicIndex bounds-checking would pass grep but fail runtime; the same for frameInfo guard ordering issues (e.g. guard added but after a side-effect statement).
findings.recommendation: Append to T12 a 'Security boundary runtime checks (15-min manual)' subsection that runs the 4 specific Web Inspector commands from round 1 Finding 5: (1) Sandbox attr: in parent context, run `document.querySelector('#insight-iframe').sandbox.toString()` — assert exactly 'allow-scripts'. Then attempt `iframe.contentWindow.parent.document.body.innerHTML = 'pwned'` — assert SecurityError thrown OR no effect on parent DOM. (2) frameInfo: temporarily inject test JS into iframe srcdoc that calls `window.webkit?.messageHandlers?.bridge?.postMessage({type: 'insightRequestSave', payload: {}})`. Verify in Console.app or Xcode Console that NO Swift handler invocation occurs (either webkit.messageHandlers is undefined per sandbox null-origin, OR frameInfo.isMainFrame guard rejects with sanitized log). (3) postMessage allowlist: in parent Web Inspector, run `window.postMessage({type: 'insightRequestNavigate', payload: {url: 'https://evil.com'}}, '*')` — assert parent's message handler rejects (no Swift call, NSLog warning visible). (4) topicIndex bounds: simulate posting `insightDeepDiveClicked` with payloads {sectionId: 'sec1', topicIndex: -1}, {topicIndex: 999}, {topicIndex: null}, {topicIndex: '5'}, {topicIndex: {}} — assert each rejected with bounds-check log. Document expected log/UI signature for each. Each test takes ~3 minutes; total ~15 min, gives runtime verification grep cannot.

findings.location: tech-spec.md Risks table 'Tests deferred — v2 surface larger than v1' (line 522)
findings.issue: Round 1 Finding 4 recommended rewriting this risk entry to (a) enumerate the 4 v2-specific risk classes (sandbox boundary, atomic disk write, ZIP path safety, parallel scheduling cap) explicitly so reviewers cannot apply v1's PASS-by-analogy verdict, and (b) make the upgrade-vs-defer question explicit (do PostMessageAllowlistTests + InsightCacheAtomicCRUDTests need to be upgraded from follow-up to pre-merge?). Round 2 edited the entry to add 'T8 explicitly performs the tasks/todo.md rewrite (removes dead v1 modules, adds v2 paths). T12 adds 4 adversarial scenarios beyond happy-path' — this acknowledges the COMPENSATION but does not enumerate the RISKS, and the explicit upgrade-vs-defer decision is still not posed. A reviewer reading this entry can still conclude 'same risks as v1, defer' without examining whether the iframe sandbox boundary or atomic write semantics warrant pre-merge tests despite Decision 9. This is minor because the underlying defenses (frameInfo + CSP + UUID dirs + cleanup) are sound, but the documentation should reflect the explicit decision.
findings.recommendation: Expand the risks-table entry: 'Tests deferred — v2 introduces 4 NEW risk classes vs v1 (NOT same risks): (a) iframe sandbox boundary (postMessage allowlist + payload schema + frameInfo guard) — silent security failure if regressed; (b) atomic disk write (rename, manifest CRUD, cleanup ordering) — silent data corruption if regressed; (c) ZIP staging path safety — UUID node IDs prevent traversal but staging dir construction order matters; (d) parallel scheduling cap — silent rate-limit cascade if regressed. Defenses: (a) frameInfo + CSP connect-src none + sandbox null-origin (3 layers); (b) per-session UUID dirs + cleanup-on-close bound blast radius to one session; (c) UUID-based node IDs eliminate user-controlled path components; (d) gated scheduling pattern proven in GraphRAG round-1 fix. Compensation: T8 rewrites tasks/todo.md with v2 paths; T12 adds 4 adversarial scenarios; pre-merge security audit (T10) hand-traces sandbox + frameInfo + escape pipeline. Explicit decision: PostMessageAllowlistTests + InsightCacheAtomicCRUDTests are NOT upgraded to pre-merge for v2 because (i) follow-up XCTest infrastructure setup is the bottleneck, (ii) per-session blast radius bound makes regression recoverable, (iii) Audit Wave + adversarial QA provides one-time gate. Re-evaluate this decision at v2 merge if Audit Wave flags any specific path.'

findings.location: tech-spec.md T1 fixture commitment (line 632) + Testing Strategy (line 478)
findings.issue: Round 1 Finding 2 recommended committing equivalent fixture coverage for v2: (i) insight-skeleton-sample.json (happy), (ii) 3+ malformed variants for fallback path (missing required field, wrong type, oversized array, recursive nesting, invalid enum value), (iii) postmessage-payloads adversarial fixtures (5+: extra fields, missing required, type confusion, oversized string, out-of-range topicIndex), (iv) pre-built stale session dir for cleanup verification. Round 2 commits ONLY (i) — the happy-path skeleton sample. The fallback path (defensive parser produces 'single prose section' fallback per Acceptance Criteria line 545) has NO committed fixture to hand-trace against; reviewers in T9/T10 cannot verify the fallback works without writing their own malformed input or running the live LLM. Similarly, postMessage payload schema validation (line 565 acceptance criterion) has no fixture — reviewers cannot trace the validation logic against concrete adversarial inputs. The committed happy fixture is genuinely useful (closes the larger gap from round 1) but the malformed/adversarial fixtures would close the remaining hand-trace gap at low cost (each fixture is ~50 lines of JSON).
findings.recommendation: Expand T1 deliverables: commit Tests/Fixtures/insight-skeleton-sample.json (already planned, keep) PLUS a new directory Tests/Fixtures/insight-skeleton-malformed/ containing at minimum 3 cases: missing-required-field.json (skeleton with no 'sections' key), wrong-type.json (sections is a string not an array), invalid-enum.json (section.type is 'unknownType' not in SectionType cases). Each fixture documented with a 1-line comment in a README.md describing the expected fallback behavior (single prose section, log warning, etc.). Optionally also commit Tests/Fixtures/postmessage-payloads/ with 3 cases: out-of-range-topicindex.json, type-confusion.json (topicIndex as string), missing-required.json (no sectionId field). T9 + T10 reviewers MUST hand-trace the parser/validator against each fixture as part of their review. Total cost: ~30 minutes to produce 6 small JSON files + README. Closes the remaining round-1 fixture gap entirely.

findings.location: tech-spec.md Task 2 (Vendor Chart.js + libs MANIFEST) line 636
findings.issue: Round 1 Finding 9 recommended adding a build-time/CI integrity check (recompute shasum -a 256 for each vendored file, fail build if MANIFEST entry doesn't match) to convert honor-system into automated gate. Round 2 Task 2 description added 'record in new MANIFEST.txt along with existing Mermaid + KaTeX + Prism versions and SHAs' — addresses the 'all libs' half but no build-time enforcement. If a developer updates MANIFEST.txt to match a tampered Chart.js, the system silently accepts it. The Verify-smoke step (`shasum -a 256 ... matches MANIFEST.txt entry`) is run once at PR review time, not on every build. This is minor because the sandbox + CSP defense-in-depth limits the blast radius of a tampered lib (it still cannot exfil via connect-src 'none' nor escape sandbox), but the chain-of-trust on vendored libs is unverified post-merge.
findings.recommendation: Add to Task 2 Files-to-modify: a new build-phase script `MarkView/Resources/Editor/vendor/verify_manifest.sh` that iterates every file referenced in MANIFEST.txt, computes shasum -a 256, compares to MANIFEST entry, exits non-zero on mismatch. Wire as Xcode 'Run Script' build phase BEFORE Compile Sources. Add to Acceptance Criteria: 'Build phase verify_manifest.sh runs on every build; tampering with vendor/ files without updating MANIFEST.txt fails build with clear error.' Total cost: ~15 minutes to write + wire the script. Eliminates honor-system trust on vendored libs.

findings.location: tech-spec.md Decision 7 (ZIP export) + T12 close-during-export scenario
findings.issue: Round 1 Finding 8 recommended T12 manual QA matrix items: (a) export immediately after root generation (1-node session), (b) double-click Save Archive within 1 second, (c) corrupt cached node + export to verify hard-fail vs partial archive. Round 2 added T12 (h) close-tab-during-in-flight-export (cancellation path). The cancellation case is valuable and was not in round 1. But the 3 round-1 cases remain uncovered: (a) empty/minimal session export, (b) concurrent export click, (c) cached-node-corruption export. Also: round 1 noted /usr/bin/zip non-zero exit codes other than 0 (zip can return 12 for nothing-to-do, 18 for could-not-open-source) — Acceptance Criteria line 597 only checks 'exits 0' and the wrapper either passes or fails uniformly. If zip returns 12 (which can happen for empty staging dir), behavior is unspecified.
findings.recommendation: Add to T12 a brief ZIP edge-case sub-matrix: (m) Export immediately after root generation (1-node session, no expansions) — verify ZIP opens and shows root only with breadcrumb empty. (n) Click Save Archive twice within 1 second — verify second click is either disabled OR queued OR runs in fresh tmp dir without collision; verify both result in correct (or one-correct-one-rejected) outcome. (o) Manually corrupt one cached node HTML (`rm` + `touch`), then export — verify either hard-fail with user-visible error containing the broken node UUID, OR partial archive with explicit warning, NOT silent success. Also amend Acceptance Criteria line 597 from 'exits 0' to 'exits 0; for non-zero exit codes (e.g. 12 for nothing-to-do), wrapper surfaces user-visible error containing exit code and sanitized stderr — does NOT silently succeed.'
